item.title: Introduction to Serger Sewing
item.description:
Learn the basics of operating our serger, the Juki MO-735!   In this class we will go over the basic operation and key functions of a serger sewing machine. Threading the machine and safety will be discussed.

Between three and five threads are routinely used to sew a seam, trim off the raw edges & finish the edges all at the same time with the Juki MO-735 serger.  However, this workshop focuses solely on learning the 4-thread overlock stitch.

This course is mandatory in order to book the serger.  Children under 13 must be accompanied by an adult.

Registration requires a library card and begins October 20, 2026 at 12:30 p.m.

item.title: Bring Your Problem: Can AI Help?
item.description:
Do you have a recurring problem you think AI might help with? A thing you keep doing by hand that feels like it should be easier? Bring it. If you don't have one, come help your neighbours with theirs.

In this interactive class with our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln, you'll learn a simple seven-step way to think about problems: what's annoying you, what you've tried, what AI could actually do, and where it would fail. We'll gather real problems from the room, sort them into groups, and map out what's worth solving with AI, and what's better solved without it. We'll also talk honestly about what an AI fix costs: your money, your time, and sometimes your private information. The problems AI could help with most are often the most personal, and the most personal ones are worth the most care.

Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program. After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

item.title: Kensington Market: Heart of the City - Documentary Screening Presented by Producer and Director Stuart Clarfield
item.description:
Kensington Market

Stuart Clarfield's feature documentary explores Kensington Market's 160-year history, from it origins as a Victorian suburb of Toronto, to its roots as a Jewish immigrant marketplace to its evolution as a cultural hub for almost every community that calls Toronto home. The film highlights the neighbourhood's vibrant identity and its ongoing struggle against gentrification and development, attempting to preserve the rich bohemian spirit of Kensington, as modern Toronto grows around it. 104 minutes (2024).

Online registration is optional, not required.

item.title: Culture and Technology Book Club : Killed by a Traffic Engineer
item.description:
The Culture and Technology Book club brings readers together every two months to discuss new and classic texts that raise important questions about the way technology transforms our cultural and political lives.

This meeting we'll discuss:

Killed by A Traffic Engineer

(also available as an audiobook)

Civil Engineering professor Wes Marshal takes a hard look at how traffic engineering standards in North America have shaped our streets for the worse. He examines some of the dubious and unscientific assumptions central to traffic engineering such as their fixation on speed. Marshal asks what it might look like to build transportation infrastructure with a more holistic understanding of people's needs. 

Register for this program to receive the discussion questions a week in advance of the meeting.

item.title: Vibe Coding: Personal Library App
item.description:
What if you could build your own personal library app, just by describing it?

In this class, you'll use an AI coding assistant to build a small app for your reading life: add books you've read and books you want to read, keep your whole list in one private place, and link each book to the library catalogue so placing a hold is one click away. You'll learn the build loop: describe what you want, review the plan, build one feature, test it, fix the bugs. Your reading list stays on your own computer. The library keeps the books; this file keeps your reading life, and it travels with you.

Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.

Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
